Measurable outcome: Every admitted patient has a documented care plan within 24 hours of admission and a doctor review on every day of the stay
Every medicine dose is checked against the doctor's order and the patient's recorded allergies before it is given.
Target: 100% of doses checked and zero harmful medication errors

Measurable outcome: Every patient leaves with a discharge summary in Sinhala, Tamil or English that explains medicines, warning signs and the follow-up date, and receives a follow-up call within 48 hours.
Target: 100% of discharges and 90% or more of follow-up calls made

Measurable outcome: The patient and family get a cost estimate at admission and one consolidated bill at discharge, without visiting separate counters.
A family member can stay with the patient overnight, with a bed or chair provided, and meals are available for the patient (to the diet ordered) and the bystander.
Patients with private or corporate insurance have pre-authorisation requested at admission and are told their expected out-of-pocket amount before treatment begins.
Target: 90% or more of insured admissions within 2 hours

Measurable outcome: A patient who needs admission is in a bed within 60 minutes of the doctor's decision and leaves within 2 hours of the discharge order.
A new admission is assessed by the ward nurse within 15 minutes of reaching the ward and by a doctor within 1 hour.
Newly prescribed in-patient medicines reach the ward within 30 minutes of the order, and urgent medicines within 10 minutes.
Every patient leaves the consultation knowing their diagnosis, treatment and follow-up plan.
Patients showing warning signs (chest pain, breathing difficulty, heavy bleeding, a feverish child, suspected dengue) are spotted at registration and sent straight to a doctor.
Target: 100% of cases identified and seen within 10 minutes

Measurable outcome: Every patient leaves with a written plan and, where needed, a booked follow-up date, so long-term conditions such as diabetes and high blood pressure are reviewed on time.
Target: 90% or more of patients needing follow-up have a date booked

Measurable outcome: A patient can book, change or cancel an appointment by phone or online in under 3 minutes.
Follow their place in the queue live.
Target: Live queue tracking at every OPD

Measurable outcome: Patients are served in Sinhala, Tamil or English at every OPD on every shift, with signs, forms and prescriptions in their language.
Elderly, pregnant and differently abled patients get priority registration, wheelchair help and step-free access.
A patient with a booked appointment sees the doctor within 15 minutes of the appointment time, and a walk-in patient within 30 minutes.
A patient with a simple illness completes registration, consultation, tests and pharmacy within 90 minutes of arrival.
A patient who calls with an urgent concern can see a doctor the same day.
Nurses check every in-patient at set intervals and record pain and comfort, so no patient is left unattended.
Target: 95% or more of scheduled rounds recorded

Measurable outcome: Nurses follow hand-hygiene steps at every patient contact, checked by monthly audits.
Every in-patient is assessed for fall and pressure-sore risk after admission, and a prevention plan is started.
Every bed has a working call bell within reach and a named nurse for each shift, shown at the bedside, who is the family's single contact for updates.

Before discharge, nurses teach the patient and bystander how to manage care at home (wound care, insulin, feeding, medicines) in their language and confirm understanding by asking them to repeat it back.
Patients and bystanders can request water, meals, linen, cleaning or a bystander bed through one nurse-station number.
Target: 100% of wards and 90% or more of requests closed within the shift

Measurable outcome: A patient's call bell is answered within 3 minutes.
Scheduled medicines are given within 30 minutes of the due time.
In the ETU, triage and vital signs are completed within 5 minutes of arrival.
Doctors explain the diagnosis, options, expected cost and plan in plain language, and patients rate "my doctor listened and explained" 4.5 out of 5 or higher.
Doctors follow national or recognised guidelines for common conditions such as dengue, diabetes, high blood pressure and asthma, and record the treatment plan in the patient file.
Every patient is told the options, risks and costs, and gives informed consent, before any procedure or surgery.
A patient can see each doctor's branch, specialty and session times online, and sessions run as published, with any change notified in advance.
Target: 95% or more of sessions run as published

Measurable outcome: Follow-up consultations can be done by telemedicine, so patients with long-term conditions or who live far from a branch do not travel for every review.
A patient's notes that test results and prescriptions are available at any Medihelp branch, so history and tests are not repeated.
Critical and urgent test results are reviewed and acted on by the doctor within 30 minutes of being reported.
An on-call specialist sees an ETU or in-patient case within 60 minutes of being called, at any hour.
A new patient can get a specialist appointment within 5 working days.
Patients feel respected and informed at registration and billing, and receive a personal response to every complaint within 7 days.
Target: Average 4.5 out of 5 or higher; 100% of complaints answered within 7 days

Measurable outcome: Patient records are kept private in line with the Personal Data Protection Act, No. 9 of 2022: only the treating team has access and every access is logged.
Target: Zero confirmed breaches and 100% of access logged

Measurable outcome: Every branch holds a valid registration as a private medical institution and all required licences.
Target: 100% of branches and renewals tracked 90 days ahead

Measurable outcome: Registration, payment and insurer or corporate-claim steps are done at one counter or digitally, and cash, card and QR payments are accepted at every branch.
Consultation fees, common test prices and room rates are displayed at registration and online, so patients know the cost before deciding.
Target: 100% of branches and updated within 7 days of any change

Measurable outcome: Medical certificates, report copies and receipts are available by SMS, WhatsApp or online without another visit.
A new patient is registered within 5 minutes and a returning patient within 2 minutes.
Calls to a branch or the hotline are answered within 30 seconds, and WhatsApp or online enquiries within 15 minutes.
Insurance and corporate claims are submitted within 1 working day of the visit or discharge.
Every prescription is checked by a pharmacist, and the customer is told the dose and timing, with no dispensing errors reaching the customer.
Target: 100% of prescriptions counselled and 99.9% or more error-free dispensing

Measurable outcome: No expired medicine is ever sold, and cold-chain items such as insulin are kept at the right temperature, with logs checked twice a day.
Target: Zero expired items sold and 100% of logs complete

Measurable outcome: No customer is charged above the NMRA maximum retail price where one is set, and a lower-cost generic is offered whenever one exists and the doctor agrees.
Target: 100% at or below the price cap and generic offered for 90% or more of eligible prescriptions

Measurable outcome: A customer finds every prescribed item in one visit, with an alternative offered when an item is out of stock.
Target: 95% or more of prescription items filled in one visit

Measurable outcome: Customers can order by phone or WhatsApp and choose home delivery or ready-for-pick-up.
Each pharmacy at an OPD/ETU branch is open whenever the OPD is open, so patients get their medicines before leaving.
A customer can find and purchase their required medicines and other items within 30 minutes of entering the pharmacy.
A prescription is dispensed within 10 minutes for up to 3 items and within 20 minutes for more.
An out-of-stock item is sourced and delivered within 24 hours (the same day from a nearby Medihelp pharmacy where possible), and the customer is told the time upfront.
Test results are accurate and reliable: every sample is correctly identified, and every quality-control check is met.
Target: Zero sample mix-ups and 100% of quality-control checks passed

Measurable outcome: The main laboratory keeps its ISO 15189 accreditation and works towards the same standard at its other laboratories, with external quality assurance results within acceptable limits.
Target: Accreditation maintained and 95% or more of external quality results within limits

Measurable outcome: Samples are collected by trained staff, with fasting and preparation instructions given in advance.
Target: 95% or more collected successfully at the first attempt and 90% or more told preparation steps in advance

Measurable outcome: A patient can give a sample at any collection centre and receive the report online or at any branch, without returning to the original centre.
Target: 95% or more of reports available online

Measurable outcome: Home sample collection can be booked, including early-morning slots for fasting tests.
Target: 95% or more collected in the booked slot

Measurable outcome: Health-check and corporate screening packages are completed in one visit with one combined report.
Urgent results (ETU and in-patient) are ready within 60 minutes and routine results within 4 hours.
During dengue season, full blood count and dengue test results for patients with fever are ready within 1 hour.
Critical results are phoned to the treating doctor within 15 minutes of being confirmed.
